key_idea: Greedily cut s into blocks each containing every alphabet letter; with k complete blocks the shortest missing subsequence has length exactly k+1, so a query is a yes iff its length is k+1 and it is not a subsequence of s.
sketch: One pass over s counts complete blocks k (reset the seen-set whenever all |v| letters have appeared). For each query, reject immediately unless |q| = k+1; otherwise test subsequence membership by per-letter sorted position lists and lower_bound, O(|q| log |s|). Total O(|s| + sum|q| log|s|). Pitfalls: fast IO for 1e6 lines, and a query longer than k+1 that is missing is still not shortest.
